blocks: Same scam. Two countries. Only one gives your money back.
In Britain, if a scammer tricks you into sending money, your bank must refund you, up to eighty-five thousand pounds. That rule started in October twenty twenty-four.
The victim's bank pays the refund, and the bank that received the money pays half of it back.
In the first nine months, the regulator says, one hundred twelve million pounds went back to victims. Eighty-eight percent of the money claimed back was returned.
In America, two senators proposed the same idea in twenty twenty-four. It did not become law.
So if you're tricked into sending money here, your refund depends on your bank.
Why that is, and what to do, is in the full case on The Rule Changed.
